doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Guessing the violinist who joined Carter's band
summary: Young cannot recall the name of a violin-playing friend who joined the band out of Boston; Brown and Kimery offer wrong guesses.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: No, we never got to play the Apollo. That's when that violin player, famous violin player, joined Chick Carter‘s band. And he went onto play with…
Keep on naming because you got to name him.
Stuff Smith? Stuff Smith? Stuff Smith.
No, not Stuff Smith. Now you‘ve done named two, now he was just as good as them two men you named. He was a little younger than they were, he also played saxophone and violin.
How can I not call it? You call. Oh, that‘s a shame, I can‘t think of these people.
Well, don‘t feel bad, I can‘t either.

He played with, he came to California and joined. Who‘s band did he play with? The band came, he was a drummer, and had that big band that left and went to New York. He was from California, the drummer.
Lionel Hampton. He played with Lionel Hampton for a short time before he passed…
Hm, violin. Young:…but he came to California, but he was good.
But he was in Chick Carter‘s band, he joined Chick Carter‘s band when you were in the band?
Yeah, he joined Chick Carter coming out of Boston, he was from originally from Boston. And he came with Chick Carter…
Is that a white fellow you mentioned?

Because that sounds like a white man‘s name. Joe Kennedy, you said? No, that was not him. Joe Kennedy. No, I‘ll tell you his name because he and I were good buddies, I can‘t think, I just my mind is doing things to me at times and then as soon as we get through talking he‘ll come, here he comes.
Well, we‘ll come, maybe this will come back to you, we‘ll plug it in tomorrow.
